diagnostic_evidence.quote: We will also show that, under specific domain decomposition parameters, in addition to scalability, the one-level Schwarz method can also achieve robustness with respect of the wavenumber.

Finally in \Cref{sec:numeric} we present two types of numerical results: first, showing that the limiting spectrum is descriptive for the convergence of the algorithm even in the case of a moderate number of domains and then on the discretised problem using the edge element method.
Secondly, we aim at showing scalability for discretised Maxwell's equation in a waveguide and decomposition into many subdomains when using different types of transmission conditions.

issues.failure_explanation: The abstract and contribution list claim a demonstration of wavenumber robustness of the one-level Schwarz method (under specific domain decomposition parameters), and the introduction and Section 4 promise a second family of numerical results on the discretised problem (edge elements, many-subdomain scalability). The paper contains neither: no theorem, proposition or experiment varies the wavenumber or establishes wavenumber robustness (the numerics only fix k=10 and k=10+i and plot spectral radii of the continuous-level iteration matrices), and no discretised/edge-element experiment appears; the numerical section ends after the limiting-spectrum subsection with the complex-wavenumber plots.

failure_location.quote: Furthermore, we demonstrate that the one-level Schwarz method can achieve robustness with respect to the wave number under specific domain decomposition parameters, offering new insights into its applicability for large-scale electromagnetic wave problems.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the claims of a wavenumber-robustness demonstration and of discretised edge-element numerical results (or explicitly mark them as forthcoming), since the source contains no such content.
issues.overall_effect: Two advertised contributions (wavenumber robustness; discretised edge-element scalability experiments) are unsupported, so the paper's stated scope and achievements are misleading.
issues.title: Advertised wavenumber-robustness result and discretised edge-element experiments are absent from the paper
issues.why_classification: Withdrawing the undelivered promises is a limited weakening that leaves the paper's actual results (modal limiting-spectrum analysis and continuous-level numerics) intact, but it removes advertised contributions, which is more than a minor local fix.

issues.failure_explanation: With xtilde = x - i*sigma*(x - a_j) for x < a_j one has Im(xtilde) = sigma*(a_j - x) > 0 in the left layer, so a left-going (outgoing) mode e^{-i*beta*xtilde} has modulus e^{beta*sigma*(a_j-x)}: it grows exponentially with depth into the layer instead of decaying. A left PML absorbing outgoing left-going modes requires Im(xtilde) < 0, i.e. xtilde = x + i*sigma*(x - a_j) for x < a_j (the right branch x + i*sigma*(x - b_j) correctly damps right-going modes). As written, the left layer contradicts the stated purpose of the PML and the symmetric construction tacitly used later, in which the single transmission eigenvalue of eq:lambdaPML is applied at both interfaces.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Flip the sign of the left branch of the stretching to xtilde = x + i*sigma*(x - a_j) for x in [a_j - ell, a_j], making the left layer absorbing and consistent with the single-eigenvalue formalism.
issues.overall_effect: The stated PML construction is non-absorbing (in fact amplifying) on the left side as written; the displayed analysis, which derives the transmission operator only from the right-hand layer, is unaffected.
issues.title: Left PML stretching has the wrong sign and amplifies outgoing waves
issues.why_classification: The repair is a one-sign local correction to the construction; no result or guarantee in the paper depends on the erroneous left branch.

The proposition claims lambda^T_i = kappa, the opposite sign. Its proof asserts lambda_TE_i = -beta_TE_i and lambda_TM_i = -k^2/beta_TM_i (missing the factor i, contradicting the limit of eq:lambdaPML) and then 'kappa = lambda^T_i', which is inconsistent even with the asserted values (for TEM, kappa = ik while the proof's own lambda_TEM_i = -ik). Consequently the stated value b^T_i = e^{-i*beta*(L+delta)}, which corresponds to lambda = +kappa, is wrong: substituting lambda = -kappa into the coefficients of prop:R-ite (or inverting M^{l,l} directly) gives b^T_i = e^{+i*beta*(L+delta)}. The same sign confusion appears in the PML section, where the text defines T as mapping E x n to ((curl E) x n) x n (the layer's Dirichlet-to-Neumann map), which would give eigenvalues +i*beta*(1+e)/(1-e), the opposite sign of eq:lambdaPML; the displayed formula (with the minus sign) is the correct one. The claims a^T_i = 0 and [I^T(i)]^N = 0 do remain valid, since the numerator of a^T_i contains (lambda^T_i)^2 - kappa^2, which vanishes for both signs.
